dimensions.assessment: Affects all consumers booking short-term lodging in interstate commerce, as well as all hotels, short-term rental operators, and online travel platforms.
dimensions.evidence: It shall be unlawful for a covered entity to display, advertise, market, or offer in interstate commerce... a price for covered services that does not clearly, conspicuously, and prominently-- (A) display the total services price...

dimensions.assessment: Changes how lodging prices are marketed and displayed across all online and traditional advertising platforms, affecting transaction transparency for consumers.
dimensions.evidence: disclose to any individual who seeks to purchase covered services the total services price at the time the covered services are first displayed...

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state federal spending or budgetary impacts, focusing instead on commercial pricing practices and legal enforcement.
Establishes a nationwide advertising standard treated as an FTC rule violation and grants enforcement powers to federal and state officials while preempting inconsistent state laws.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of subsection (a) shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice prescribed under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act...

dimensions.assessment: Permanent federal regulatory standard taking effect 450 days after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The prohibition under subsection (a) shall take effect 450 days after the date of the enactment of this Act...

missing_information: Estimated federal enforcement costs for the Federal Trade Commission.
importance_detail.rationale: Prohibits deceptive lodging price advertising by requiring hotels, short-term rentals, and third-party online sellers to display the total services price upfront, enforced by the FTC and state attorneys general.
